subject: Ghanaian Language
name: JHS 3 Ghanaian Language
description: The JHS 3 Ghanaian Language curriculum consolidates knowledge in customs, oral language, reading, grammar, and writing. It focuses on marriage rites, naming systems, the clan system, traditional government, advanced conversation, reading comprehension, translation, grammar usage, and composition writing.

strands.title: CUSTOMS AND INSTITUTIONS
strands.description: Understanding rites of passage, naming systems, clans, and chieftaincy.

subStrands.title: RITES OF PASSAGE: MARRIAGE
subStrands.description: Exploring marriage rites and their significance.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate an understanding of marriage of their culture and compare with other cultures of Ghana

indicators.description: Discuss the processes involved in performing marriage rites in their culture

exemplars.description: Explain what marriage is
Read and discuss a text on marriage
Identify types of marriage
Identify some of the marriage rites in their culture and write them
Discuss marriage rites performance
Explore the significance of the processes involved in performing marriage rites

indicators.description: Compare and contrast the marriage rites in their culture to other cultures in Ghana

exemplars.description: Present marriage rites among their people
Relate the marriage rites of their culture to those of other Ghanaian cultures

indicators.description: Compare and contrast the traditional marriage rites to the contemporary marriage rites and dramatise both

exemplars.description: Explain some of the contemporary marriage rites in their culture
Compare and contrast the traditional to the contemporary marriage rites
Dramatise marriage rites session of their culture

subStrands.title: NAMING SYSTEMS - CIRCUMSTANTIAL, REINCARNATION, DEITY NAMES
subStrands.description: Understanding circumstantial, reincarnation, and deity names.

contentStandards.description: Exhibit knowledge of the understanding and application of circumstantial, reincarnation and deity names

indicators.description: Identify and discuss circumstances that result in naming children in their community

exemplars.description: Explain circumstances that lead to circumstantial names
Write some of the names and relate them to the circumstances
Discuss the significance of circumstantial names

indicators.description: Discuss reincarnation names and their meanings

exemplars.description: Identify reincarnation names and discuss their meanings
Discuss the significance of reincarnation names

indicators.description: Identify and discuss deity names

exemplars.description: Explain circumstances that lead to giving new borns deity names (e.g. Akan: Tutu, Antoa; Ewe: Afram, Klu)
Discuss the significance of deity names

subStrands.title: THE CLAN SYSTEM
subStrands.description: Understanding trends and factors affecting the clan system.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding and knowledge of the factors that militate against the clan system

indicators.description: Discuss trends affecting the clan system

exemplars.description: Identify and discuss the trends affecting the clan system
Discuss ways by which the clan system can be strengthened
Discuss the similarities and differences between the various clan systems in their locality

contentStandards.description: Exhibit knowledge and understanding of the traditional governing structure (chief/queenmother, chief priest, traditional military, sub chiefs, king makers) of their society and their duties

indicators.description: Explore the traditional governing structure of their community and discuss the duties of the functionaries

exemplars.description: Read and discuss a text on traditional governance
Identify the traditional governing structure of their community
Discuss and write down the duties of the functionaries
Discuss and write the importance of the functionaries

subStrands.title: CONVERSATION/EVERYDAY DISCOURSE
subStrands.description: Using appropriate language in various contexts.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate use of appropriate language orally in specific situations

indicators.description: Use appropriate register in everyday communication (informal and formal) with diverse partners on grade-level topics/texts/issues

exemplars.description: Identify some slang words and jargons accepted locally and internationally
Use everyday, informal topics and situations that are more appropriate for the use of slang and jargon
Create and act scenes on texts/issues/topics using both formal and informal register to distinguish characters

indicators.description: Ask questions that link the ideas of several speakers and respond to others' questions in a discussion

exemplars.description: Use open ended questions to enable speaker link ideas of other speakers on topics/issues
Listen attentively to view points on topics/issues in a conversation and respond appropriately
Engage in conversations on topics/issues with several speakers and respond to different views

indicators.description: Use appropriate language orally to discuss grade-level national issues fluently

exemplars.description: Identify grade-level national issues (the youth in agriculture, sanitation, life style diseases, free SHS, etc.)
Discuss grade-level national issues in detail using appropriate register

indicators.description: Express opinions and advice on a range of everyday issues and situations clearly

exemplars.description: Identify a range of everyday issues e.g. road/domestic accidents, domestic violence, child abuse
Engage in conversations on these issues giving your opinion and advice

indicators.description: Demonstrate appropriate turn taking and use techniques for effective argument (debate)

exemplars.description: Identify interesting topics/issues appropriate for argument and debate
Observe and use the skills of turn taking in arguments and debates

subStrands.title: LISTENING COMPREHENSION
subStrands.description: Listening to and discussing complex texts.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate the ability to listen to extended reading and identify key information

indicators.description: Listen to a more natural level-appropriate interactions with multiple speakers for example, TV shows, dramas, films, etc.

exemplars.description: Discuss and write key information e.g. message, theme, tone, mood in level appropriate texts/speeches
Listen to and compare information written from texts/speeches

indicators.description: Initiate and participate in meaningful and collaborative discussions on texts and related materials building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively

exemplars.description: Listen to and identify key issues in level appropriate texts/speeches/dialogues
Initiate discussions on ideas and share opinions on level appropriate texts/speeches/dialogues
Engage in conferences to discuss ideas noted from texts/speeches/dialogues and express their own clearly and persuasively

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding in the use of the basic tones correctly in speaking and reading

indicators.description: Apply the idea of tones correctly when speaking and reading in contexts

exemplars.description: Engage in a conversation on a given topic using the basic tones correctly
Read sentences using the correct tones
Read a passage using the correct tone patterns to depict the right context

contentStandards.description: Describe their everyday experiences on more complex topics using appropriate presentational skills

indicators.description: Discuss complex topics related to everyday activities

exemplars.description: Read a text on deforestation in Ghana, same sex marriage, insecurity, etc.
Discuss some of the everyday activities in the factory, traditional occupational shops, settlement of cases at the palace, etc.

indicators.description: Compose their own group report on some topical issues

exemplars.description: Develop their own report on a range of suitable familiar and unfamiliar, concrete and abstract topics
Make a presentation on the topics above to the class for discussion

contentStandards.description: Read longer passages silently, identify main ideas, answer questions and summarise the passage

indicators.description: Locate the main and subsidiary points in a range of texts and rewrite logically with accuracy in their own words

exemplars.description: Read and understand a passage of between 200-250 words from different subject areas silently
Identify the main ideas in the passage
Rewrite the ideas logically in their own words
Answer recall, meaning and inferential questions based on the passage

indicators.description: Summarise passages read in given number of sentences

exemplars.description: Arrange the main ideas in a range of passages logically and coherently
Summarise a passage of two hundred words in fifty words

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of translating texts from source language to the target language

indicators.description: Decode the meaning of texts and translate from source to target language

exemplars.description: Translate texts of about one hundred words from source to a target language
Read and discuss the translated text

subStrands.title: INTEGRATING GRAMMAR IN WRITTEN LANGUAGE (NOUNS, ADJECTIVES)

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of the use of singular and plural nouns in sentences and passages

indicators.description: Discuss nouns under singular and plural forms in an increasing and abstract range of texts

exemplars.description: Identify and classify nouns in a passage according to their singular and plural forms
Construct simple and compound sentences with the singular and plural nouns in speech and in writing

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of how adjectives are combined in a sentence

indicators.description: Discuss how adjectives follow each other in a sentence

exemplars.description: Identify adjectives in texts
Form sentences with two or three adjectives

subStrands.title: INTEGRATING GRAMMAR IN WRITTEN LANGUAGE (VERBS, ADVERBS)

contentStandards.description: Exhibit knowledge and understanding of the use of auxiliary verbs

indicators.description: Discuss auxiliary verbs in sentences

exemplars.description: Identify types of verbs in a recorded/read passage
Discuss auxiliary verbs (where applicable)
Construct sentences with auxiliary verbs

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of how adverbs are combined in a sentence

indicators.description: Discuss how adverbs follow each other in a sentence

exemplars.description: Identify adverbs in texts
Construct sentences with two or three adverbs correctly

strands.title: COMPOSITION WRITING
strands.description: Structuring and organizing ideas in compositions.

subStrands.title: STRUCTURE AND ORGANISE IDEAS IN COMPOSITION WRITING

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the features of the various text types discussed and use the knowledge to write a coherent essay on the text types

indicators.description: Plan and structure a range of extended texts using paragraphs to show progression from one idea to the next and linking paragraphs using cohesive language

exemplars.description: Write a coherent essay on any of the text types (e.g. narrative, descriptive, creative, academic, and argumentative and letter writing) on a given topic
Identify and write the topic and supporting sentences in the paragraphs

strands.title: LITERATURE
strands.description: Exploring drum language, prose, poetry, and drama.

subStrands.title: DRUM/HORN/XYLOPHONE LANGUAGE, PROSE, POETRY AND DRAMA

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate an understanding of drum language, appellations and war songs

indicators.description: Explore drum language/appellations and war songs respectively

exemplars.description: Describe the features of drum language/appellation
Discuss drum language/appellation
Discuss the occasions/situations on/in which drum language/appellation is used
State the importance of drum language/appellation
Appreciate war songs in your language
Discuss the importance of war songs

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding in the writer's use of language in a prose, poetry and drama texts

indicators.description: Discuss how writers use language to create effect in an increasing range of prose, poetry and drama

exemplars.description: Discuss characterisation in relation to prose, poetry and drama texts and give examples from texts
Explore ways that writers use a wide range of literary devices (personification, alliteration, assonance) in a range of prose, poetry and drama texts
Discuss how writers use settings to create different effects in a range of prose, poetry and drama
Discuss how writers use language to create mood and tone in an increasing range of prose, poetry and drama
Discuss the ways writers structure texts in a range of prose, poetry and drama texts
